direct_answer:
SBM Offshore states it conducted a Double Materiality Assessment (DMA) in 2023 in line with the CSRD/ESRS double materiality principle, covering impacts, risks and opportunities across its own operations and upstream and downstream value chain. The process comprised: (1) stakeholder mapping and creation of a long list of topics using external sources and standards (e.g., GRI, SASB, IPIECA and ESRS draft) and selecting stakeholders for engagement based on “relevance, expertise, impact and interest”; (2) impact materiality scoring via an “extensive questionnaire” where internal experts ranked actual/potential, positive/adverse impacts across 23 topics using scope, scale, irremediability and likelihood, with a methodology designed based on SBM Offshore’s ERM risk matrix; (3) financial materiality assessment by strategy, risk, finance and sustainability professionals aligned to existing risk/financial analysis processes and thresholds and considering analyses per capital (financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social & relationship, natural); (4) cross-referencing impact and financial scores and applying a materiality threshold to determine “double material” topics; and (5) validation with key internal/external stakeholders and senior management, with Management Board approval and presentation to the Supervisory Board. Engagement for validation included unrecorded video calls to allow stakeholders to freely express views on impact materiality. SBM Offshore also notes the DMA is renewed every four years with interim updates, and Management Board members consult and validate outcomes for strategy/performance management. [Source 1][Source 4][Source 2][Source 6]

From both an impact and a financial perspective, SBM Offshore ultimately reports six ESRS material topics (following a 2024 update to better align with ESRS): Emissions; Decommissioning; Our People; Health, Safety and Security; Human Rights; and Ethics and Compliance. [Source 4][Source 6]
compliance_rationale: The passages provide a clear, step-based description of the DMA, including separate impact and financial materiality assessments, criteria used for impact scoring (scope, scale, irremediability, likelihood), thresholding to determine double materiality, and stakeholder engagement/validation with Management Board approval. They also identify the final ESRS material topics. However, the evidence does not explicitly list which matters are material specifically “from both an impact and a financial perspective” beyond stating that a threshold was applied to determine “double material” topics and then listing six ESRS material topics; the detailed mapping of each topic to both dimensions (and the underlying IROs) is not included in the retrieved passages. [Source 1][Source 4][Source 6]
disclosure_gaps: Explicit confirmation (topic-by-topic) that each of the six ESRS material topics is material on both impact and financial dimensions (not only overall ESRS material), including the underlying impact and financial scores/results. [Source 1][Source 4][Source 6]
The qualitative/quantitative threshold values or cut-offs used to determine materiality (only that a threshold was applied is disclosed). [Source 1][Source 4]
Details on how interdependencies between impact and financial materiality were assessed (only that scores were cross-referenced). [Source 1][Source 4]

More specific evidence of engagement with affected stakeholders (beyond general stakeholder categories and validation calls) and how their input changed prioritisation/outcomes. [Source 4][Source 14][Source 3]

A complete list of the 23 topics assessed and which were screened out vs. retained as double material (only some non-ESRS business/strategic topics and the final six ESRS topics are mentioned). [Source 1][Source 4]

Explicit description of how due diligence outcomes informed the DMA prioritisation beyond general statements that engagements/assessments help identify and manage impacts/risks/opportunities. [Source 6][Source 11][Source 3]
key_findings: SBM Offshore conducted a DMA in 2023 aligned to CSRD/ESRS, covering own operations and upstream/downstream value chain. [Source 6][Source 5]

DMA steps included: stakeholder mapping/long-listing using external standards; impact materiality scoring by internal experts using scope/scale/irremediability/likelihood; financial materiality assessment aligned to existing risk/financial processes and capitals; cross-referencing scores and applying a threshold; and validation with stakeholders and Management Board approval. [Source 1][Source 4]

Stakeholder engagement is described as a backbone of the DMA, with examples of engagement with clients, suppliers, employees and shareholders included in the DMA process; validation involved unrecorded video calls. [Source 14][Source 4]
Management Board approved the DMA outcome and presented it to the Supervisory Board; SBM Offshore renews the materiality assessment every four years with interim updates. [Source 4][Source 2]

After a 2024 update to better align with ESRS, SBM Offshore reports six final ESRS material topics: Emissions, Decommissioning, Our People, Health, Safety and Security, Human Rights, Ethics and Compliance. [Source 4][Source 6]
